transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Grace Lin (Horizon CISO), Tom Becker (Horizon Head of Platform), Aisha Khan (Horizon Privacy Counsel)

Summary (auto):
High-level security and privacy review focused on data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI safeguards, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and confirmation that Redwood does not use customer data to train models. Customer requested details on retention windows and on-prem/VPC options for deeper control.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO attestations, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM integration, RBAC & SSO (SAML), audit logging granularity, data residency, prompt/content retention, PII/PHI handling, training-on-customer-data confirmation.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Maya, AE on the Horizon account, and with me is Diego from our SE team.
[00:08] Diego: Hi all, morning — afternoon — depending where you're joining, quick agenda, we'll run through our security docs, then dig into the data handling stuff you flagged.
[00:15] Grace: Thanks, Maya. We wanted to cover retention and PII stuff upfront, also curious about encryption and KMS options for Dedicated/Private.
[00:23] Tom: And timeline — we have a tight pilot window and need to lock in whether we can satisfy our compliance folks.
[00:28] Aisha: I'll mainly be listening for anything that affects privacy/regulatory obligations, PHI handling.

[02:05] Diego: Quick note — we'll drop links in the follow-up: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and our security questionnaire answers. For encryption, Redwood supports TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; for Dedicated and Private deployments you can integrate your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or even a customer HSM.
[02:35] Grace: When you say "integrate KMS," do you mean we can bring our own keys and you never see plaintext keys?
[02:40] Diego: Yes, BYOK — the control plane never holds your customer-managed keys; we use wrapped keys and tokenizes the material. For Private on-prem installs, keys remain entirely under your control.
[03:10] Grace: Good. How about audit logs — can we get per-request logs, including tokenization and who accessed what?
[03:18] Diego: We provide detailed audit logs for admin actions and API calls, and you can stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, S3). Logs include request metadata, model variant, latency, and status codes; we can also surface user identity if you wire SSO.

[05:05] Tom: Do logs include prompt contents by default? That's a big one for us.
[05:12] Maya: Short answer: retention and whether raw prompts are stored is configurable. For Hosted default we keep short-term logs for debugging (configurable retention), but for Dedicated/Private you can turn off retention or keep logs in your VPC only.
[05:30] Grace: Can you put concrete numbers on "short-term" for hosted?
[05:34] Diego: Default hosted retention is 30 days for prompts and responses in logs; non-production data like request traces are 7 days — but both are configurable with enterprise contracts.
[06:00] Aisha: And PII / PHI — will data ever be used to train models or appear in training corpora? Our legal team typically requires affirmative confirmation.
[06:12] Maya: We do not use customer data to train our models. Redwood explicitly does not take customer prompt/response data to update model weights. We use anonymized telemetry for service quality metrics, but not for model training.
[06:28] Grace: That's helpful. Is that in the contract?
[06:30] Maya: Yes — we'll include a clause in the DPA and the security pack; I'll send the exact language.
[07:05] Tom: You mentioned anonymized telemetry — can you clarify what is anonymized and whether it could leak PII?
[07:12] Diego: Sure. Telemetry is aggregated metrics and performance traces; any string content is redacted unless explicitly captured for debugging. If a customer sends a support request and attaches logs, those logs can be exported with consent.
[07:30] Grace: Is there an automated PII redaction feature?
[07:35] Diego: We offer configurable redaction rules for common PII patterns (emails, SSNs, phone numbers). You can enable server-side redaction before storage or configure client-side filters. For PHI, we recommend pre-processing before sending to the API or using Private deployment for max control.

[09:20] Aisha: From a compliance standpoint, if we run the pilot on Hosted with 30-day retention, does that meet HIPAA requirements?
[09:27] Maya: Hosted is trickier for HIPAA unless we sign BAAs and ensure specific controls. Redwood does offer BAAs for enterprise customers but many healthcare customers choose Dedicated or Private to keep data in their VPC or on-prem. We can scope a BAA if you want to pursue Hosted.
[09:50] Tom: Is there an SLA difference between Hosted and Dedicated?
[09:55] Maya: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput and multiple zones options; Hosted is multi-tenant with standard availability guarantees. We'll include SLA language in the pilot docs.

[12:00] Grace: About RBAC and SSO — can we map our Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[12:06] Diego: Yes. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; you can map Okta groups to roles in Redwood (viewer, operator, admin). You can also create custom roles for least privilege.
[12:25] Grace: Are audit events tied to the originating Okta user?
[12:28] Diego: Yes, when SSO is configured, audit logs include user identifiers and action performed.

[14:10] Tom: Data residency — we need data stored in the EU for EU subjects. Is that doable?
[14:16] Maya: Absolutely. We have region options for Hosted and you can specify EU-only data residency. For Dedicated and Private you can run in your preferred cloud region or on-prem.
[14:30] Grace: How do you isolate backups and caches?
[14:34] Diego: Backups and KV caches are region-scoped; for Dedicated we pin storage to the chosen region and backups are encrypted and stored in the same region by default. For Private you control backup targets.

[17:05] Aisha: Any third-party subprocessors we should list? Our procurement needs a list for vendor review.
[17:12] Maya: We'll attach the subprocessors list in the follow-up; common ones include our cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP), monitoring providers, and auditing tools.

[18:40] Grace: If we wanted to run a short POC with PHI-like test data, what is the recommended setup?
[18:46] Diego: Recommend Dedicated pilot in your VPC with BYOK and server-side redaction enabled. That way you retain control of keys and logs, and we can set retention to minimal.
[19:05] Tom: How long to spin that up?
[19:08] Diego: For a small pool we can provision a Dedicated test cluster in about 5 business days once we have access and the baseline config. We'll supply a checklist.

[21:00] Grace: There was also a question on whether you store KV cache content — if someone's prompt references PHI, is that cached somewhere?
[21:08] Diego: KV cache for autoregressive context can be configured to not persist beyond session; by default caches are ephemeral and stored in memory for inference speed; persistent caches are optional and can be disabled.
[21:25] Grace: That's reassuring.

[24:00] Maya: Quick note — our policy on training again: Redwood does not train on customer-entered prompts or responses. We can provide contractual language and the security team can endorse that.
[24:15] Aisha: Will you confirm that to be included in the DPA?
[24:19] Maya: Yes. We'll add explicit no-training clause and clarifying language about telemetry.

[26:40] Tom: For encryption at rest, do you support HSM attestations or FIPS modules?
[26:46] Diego: For enterprise customers we can integrate with FIPS-compliant KMS/HSMs and provide attestation metadata; depends on the cloud provider's offering. For private on-prem, you can provide hardware HSM.

[29:05] Grace: On logs forwarding — we asked about sending logs to our SIEM — is that push or pull?
[29:12] Diego: We can push via secure syslog or forward to an S3 bucket you control. It's configurable. We also support an API to pull logs.

[31:00] Aisha: Any known gaps in your compliance posture we should be aware of?
[31:06] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; for very specific certifications (e.g., HITRUST) we don't presently hold HITRUST, but we can work with you on compensating controls.

[33:40] Tom: If we do Dedicated with BYOK, how do key rotations work? Who performs the rotation?
[33:47] Diego: You retain control — rotation happens in your KMS. Redwood supports key rotation by referencing key aliases; we recommend rotating according to your policy; we ensure wrapped keys are re-wrapped when alias changes. We'll share a rotation guide.

[36:00] Grace: About retention, if we want zero retention of prompts and responses, is that possible?
[36:06] Diego: Yes, for Dedicated/Private you can configure zero retention (no logs stored). For Hosted we can configure short retention or opt you into a no-retention plan under enterprise agreement.
[36:20] Aisha: If zero retention is set, what happens to debugging and support?
[36:24] Maya: For support troubleshooting we'd ask you to temporarily enable capture or to share traces you collect. We don't automatically keep debug logs beyond the retention you set.

[38:15] Grace: One more on training — do you ever run internal model tuning with synthetic or customer-derived prompts?
[38:22] Diego: No customer-derived data is used for tuning. Internal models are trained on public and licensed corpora; any internal evals use synthetic data or redacted prompts. We'll provide the formal statement.

[40:50] Tom: Ok sounds good. Can you confirm timeline for deliverables?
[40:55] Maya: I'll send the SOC 2, ISO cert, subprocessors list, and security questionnaire by Monday (2026-05-25). Diego will follow with pilot docs and KMS integration steps by 2026-05-28.
[41:10] Grace: Great. We'll review and confirm whether we need a BAA and confirm data residency.

[43:00] Aisha: Thanks all, nothing else from privacy for now.
[43:05] Maya: Thanks everyone — quick recap, we'll follow up with docs and pilot config, and we'll include explicit no-training contract language.
[43:15] Diego: I'll also share a short checklist for Dedicated pilot.
[43:20] Grace: Appreciate it.

- Maya to send SOC 2 / ISO / subprocessors / security questionnaire (due 2026-05-25)
